source.title: Dictionary-Aligned Concept Control for Safeguarding Multimodal LLMs
source.authors: Jinqi Luo; Jinyu Yang; Tal Neiman; Lei Fan; Bing Yin; S. Tran; Mubarak Shah; René Vidal

record.file_problem: Whole paper and supplementary material are present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse autoencoders to multimodal LLM activations and reports reconstruction and training results, extending indirect evidence about SAE-recoverable features to MLLMs. It does not test toy-model superposition.
record.gate_note: Rows cover SAE reconstruction and training results relevant to whether sparse features are recoverable in MLLM activations. Safety-benchmark and utility outcomes for steering, per-token cost, dictionary-neighbor purity, and concept-geometry visualizations are not rows for the tested version: they do not measure SAE feature recovery as named in V4. Results attributed to cited studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: This is a safety-steering paper (DACO) that uses SAEs as a tool. Its SAE results (Table 6, Fig. 5b, Fig. 7) benchmark the authors' concept-dictionary initialization against default-initialized L1 and TopK SAEs, and use atom annotation to support steering. It never asks whether MLLM activations contain superposed or sparse features, or whether neurons are polysemantic. There is no dense, random or neuron-basis comparison, so reconstruction fidelity is not offered as evidence for V4. The paper is not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but misplaces the emphasis. The main conclusion is that DACO (a concept dictionary plus a dictionary-initialized, auto-annotated SAE) improves MLLM safety on MM-SafetyBench and JailbreakV across QwenVL, LLaVA and InternVL, while preserving utility at modest overhead. Better SAE training and concept-level analysis are supporting contributions.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops and evaluates dictionary-initialized SAEs and activation steering for MLLM safety, rather than reproducing Toy Models of Superposition or its toy-network interventions and geometry measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported SAE reconstruction and alignment results vary with SAE type (L1 versus TopK), dictionary initialization, and layer. Figure 5b also describes training-convergence differences across Qwen2.5-VL-7B and LLaVA1.6-Mistral-7B.

fits_no_version.finding: Concept-dictionary initialization of SAE decoders raises FVE on MLLM residual activations (e.g. L1 0.762→0.830, TopK 0.865→0.903 at layer 19). Decoder orthogonality stays low (~0.014–0.022).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initializing SAE decoders with supervised concept directions improves SAE reconstruction on MLLM activations.

record.code_released: not stated; the authors say they will release the steering pipeline, concept dataset, and trained SAE models.
record.peer_reviewed: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (venue stated in study metadata)
record.problems: The Table 6 caption and surrounding text do not identify its target model. SAE reconstruction scores and a few qualitative matches do not establish that SAE features are complete, stable, canonical, or representative of all MLLM features; no direct test of superposition geometry or feature interference is provided.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Steering safety/utility comparisons, over-refusal rates, dictionary-neighbor purity, concept-vector UMAP geometry, and SAE decoder orthogonality/dead-neuron metrics were left out because they do not directly measure SAE feature recovery as named in V4.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweeps or superposition geometry.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity analysis.
SAEs are used as a tool. Nothing tests whether features are spread across neurons, or whether SAE recovery reflects real sparse features (no dense or random baseline).
No test of SAE feature completeness, stability across seeds or canonicality.
No comparison of 1-D vs multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests'/T3 call and its V4 'supports' label are not justified. The SAE numbers benchmark the authors' own initialization, and the paper draws no superposition conclusions. Table 6's target model is not explicitly stated. Excluding the safety, purity and UMAP results from rows is fine.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-count-versus-dimension sweep, feature sparsity sweep, interference measure, or regular superposition geometry is tested.
Does not test whether neuron polysemanticity arises from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity indicates superposition.
Tests SAE reconstruction and training on MLLM activations, but not whether features are spread across neurons, nor their prevalence or recovery across a broad range of models and feature types.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features or test whether superposed features are 1-D directions.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Inspected top SAE atoms activated by adversarial prompts and matched them to nearest curated concept vectors.
rows.measure: Qualitative semantic alignment of activated SAE atoms with prompt intent
rows.value: Text states that the most activated atoms align with prompt intent; examples include matches to “computer system”, “aggressiveness”, and “violence”.
rows.note: Qualitative examples only; no aggregate accuracy or independent feature-label validation is reported here.
rows.check: Three cherry-picked qualitative queries, offered as evidence of their annotation's semantic grounding. Labels come from nearest concept vectors, not independent feature interpretation. No aggregate measure.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Reported SAE reconstruction and training results; qualitative Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct prompt-decomposition examples
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports substantial reconstruction FVE and directional alignment for trained SAEs, and describes activated atoms matching prompt intent (T6-Q15-L1-FVE, T6-Q15-L1-DA, T6-Q17-L1-FVE, T6-Q17-L1-DA, T6-Q19-L1-FVE, T6-Q19-L1-DA, corresponding TopK rows, F5-Qwen-L1, F5-Qwen-TopK, F5-LLaVA-L1, F5-LLaVA-TopK, F7-SAE-semantic). This is indirect evidence of SAE-recoverable features in the tested MLLM settings.
